Replacing height by the affine cap margin leaves integer bases unchanged and scales each original fiber length by the absolute continuous coefficient. The true transformed continuous first moment is zero even when the base centroid is noninteger.

All positive integer interval fibers are consecutive. Crossing every such fiber gives lower and upper heights a_i,b_i≥0, concave on that range by convexity of the body. Fibers with zero length contribute zero to the moment and mass.

Integrating each interval gives the exact equality of the two square sums, each positive. Cauchy–Schwarz on one height sequence and the finite concave square ratio on the other yield A≤κ_N B, and reversing their roles covers the opposite closed side. Nonvertical fiber boundaries have zero length, including tangent cases.

The symmetric equality witness is an actual hull and has equal square sums three, yielding the true centroid and the claimed ratio. The proper-crossing perturbation retains square sums three since 2ε²+(3−2ε²)=3. For 0<ε<1 its middle upper endpoint is above the two equal positive outer endpoints, so midpoint compatibility and all positive crossings persist.

overlap.comparison: The accepted unrestricted all-cap theorem requires an integer-base centroid and gives a weaker strict one-third bound. The frozen fixed-cap theorem allows a noninteger base, assumes every positive fiber meets the plane and improves the constant.

Its no-full-fiber condition can allow missed fibers and still requires an integer centroid base. The frozen crossing condition permits a tangent full fiber and gives a different quantitative conclusion.

Translate its common-floor minimizer at r=1+√3 down by one to obtain the frozen equality witness. The accepted theorem certifies the corresponding three-fiber cap and centroid, while the frozen lower bound extends to all N and all crossing planes.

readability: The conclusion is about a fixed cap and its opposite under the crossing hypothesis. General halfspace depth at a centroid can also involve caps that miss entire fibers.
review_method: Independent cold read of the frozen statement and proof, followed by source and exact predecessor comparison. Exact rational checks supplement the proof when arithmetic is relevant.
summary: The crossing hypothesis produces two nonnegative concave height sequences of equal square sum, giving the sharp universal bound with the stated tangency and proper-crossing behavior.
